business_quality_reasoning: Established since 2015 with 80 Google reviews at 4.9, a company number and VAT number displayed, and real project photos including higher-end garden lighting work. Micro accounts suggest a small operation, but the work shown is premium residential.
price_point_reasoning: The gallery emphasis on garden lighting design and installations suggests project work worth several hundred pounds per job rather than small call-outs.
modernity_gap: A serviceable Squarespace build with nice photos, but it reads like a brochure from several years ago with almost no conversion structure.
site_weaknesses: Phone number doubling as the hero headline - no clear statement of what services are offered or where
No quote form, service pages summary or clear next step beyond a phone number and a Contact Us button
Mobile hero is a wall of text with no call-to-action visible above the fold
Copy written from the business's perspective ('Customer Satisfaction' section reads like terms and conditions, not a benefit)
Thin homepage - satisfaction blurb, gallery teaser and two testimonials, then done
site_analysis: Warner has genuinely good assets - real garden lighting photos, named testimonials and proper company credentials in the footer - but the Squarespace page underneath them is thin and unfocused. The hero headline is a phone number, there is no service breakdown or quote flow, and mobile visitors get text and a photo with nothing to act on.
review_summary: You have beautiful project photos and genuinely lovely customer quotes, but your website does not do enough with them. Right now visitors see a phone number and a couple of pictures with no clear list of services or easy way to ask for a quote, so people who would happily pay for your lighting work may never get in touch. A clearer site would let your workmanship do the selling.
outreach_angle: Your garden lighting photos are genuinely impressive - it is a shame the site around them gives visitors almost nothing to act on.
